why: Values must be erased in non-decreasing order, so all copies of the smallest value go first, then the next value, and so on. Within one value group the pointer sweeps from one extreme member to the other, so after each group it ends at the leftmost or the rightmost member: a two-state DP over groups. Move costs count only surviving elements between positions, which a Fenwick tree of alive flags answers in O(log n); that is where this week's Fenwick tree comes in.
hints: Erasures are forced in value order. For one group of equal values, where can the pointer be when the group is finished?

To erase a group spread between positions g1 and gk, go to one end and sweep to the other, erasing as you pass. So the group ends at g1 or gk: keep dp[end] = cheapest moves so far, two states per group.

Distance between two positions = number of alive elements strictly between them that are not being erased on the way; get it from a Fenwick tree over alive flags, then delete the group from the tree. Total = n erasures + DP moves. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Erased elements no longer cost a move; distances must use survivors only, not raw index differences.
After an erase the pointer jumps to a neighbour for free, so erasing while sweeping does not cost extra moves.
Each group must try both sweep directions from both previous end states; a single greedy direction can be wrong.
Moves can total more than 2^31 for n = 10^5; use 64-bit in other languages.
statement:
You have an array arr and a pointer on its first element. Each operation costs 1 and is one of:

  • move the pointer to the previous surviving element,
  • move the pointer to the next surviving element,
  • erase the element under the pointer. The pointer then lands on the previous or the next surviving element (your choice, no extra cost).

You must erase every element, and the values you erase, in erase order, must be non-decreasing. Return the minimum total number of operations (moves plus erasures).

Worked example: arr = [2, 1, 3, 3, 2], pointer on the first 2.

  • Move right to 1 (1 move) and erase it; land back on the first 2.
  • Erase that 2; land on the first 3.
  • Move right twice, past both 3s, to the last 2 (2 moves) and erase it; land on the second 3.
  • Erase the second 3, land on the first 3, erase it.
  • 3 moves + 5 erasures = 8.
